# Wave030 FIRST — a pair proxy may abstain

15 October2026. Independent blind FIRST; no peer030 read. **Zero novelty/IDs:** refine HYP141/FA01 and its existing66-screen accounting, with wave011/013 selection/closure caveats. October final is already revealed and supplies no new selection panel.

**Mechanism.** Freeze ≤12 legal parents, target-free bins/coarse B context c, tie order and smoothing. On earlier mature train labels estimate joint, singleton and context probability tables; evaluate them on a later, user-disjoint screen panel. For observed binary y use clipped probabilities p∈[ε,1−ε] and row contrast ψ=log p(y|x,z,c)−log p(y|x,c)−log p(y|z,c)+log p(y|c). With true probabilities its expectation is interaction information; fitted tables give only a predictive proxy, not exact conditional utility given B41. Aggregate rows with1/|Cq|, then queries; retain empty/zero-positive domains explicitly rather than selecting future buyers.

For fixed predictors and conditionally independent user clusters, let d_u average ψ over that user's queries, a_u=n_u/Q and L=log((1−ε)/ε). A simultaneous one-sided lower bound is Σa_ud_u−4L√[log(66/α)Σa_u²/2]. Select no pair unless its bound exceeds0. Repeated queries do not create independent users. If independence is unjustified, this is no valid p-value; defer statistical promotion. This bound concerns expected proxy score, not true synergy or ranking gain.

**Sources/adaptation.** [IIFE2024](https://arxiv.org/html/2409.04665v1) screens interaction information, then repeatedly evaluates constructed features; it does not eliminate downstream fits. [Hoeffding1963 publisher abstract](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/01621459.1963.10500830) requires bounded independent summands. The weighted bound/held-out count-table screen are our adaptation; full theorem text was not accessed.

**Prediction/falsifier — UNRUN.** Fixed ≤128 invented rows,12 parents,≤16 user clusters and four worlds: XOR, duplicate/redundant parents, independent noise and a repeated-user rare-positive burst. Independent literal/oracle probabilities check ψ signs and the weighting/bound algebra. XOR should have positive point score even when its conservative bound abstains; no legal XOR-capable child means no admission. Duplicating queries inside one cluster must not masquerade as more independent support. Failure of these checks rejects the proxy; all-pairs abstention is allowed. Proposed15CPU/30wall seconds/128MiB, zero native/fits/Y; no execution/grant.

**Control/cost/task1 benefit.** Future pair-first, marginal-first and seeded controls share legal grammar, applicability/closure, query weights and downstream opportunities; compatible strong B/W remain primary quality references. Charge66 supervised pair looks,66 joint+12 singleton+1 context learned tables, binning/source/support materialization, every child/rejection, shared physical work once, per-policy search/scoring, failures and any later fits. No66CatBoostfits are needed, but table estimation is learned computation. Rare support, clipping, misspecification or existing CatBoost interactions may erase benefit. Utility/actual cost require a separately reserved untouched panel; no current recipe,018 prerequisite or quality claim changes.

# Wave030 B FIRST — pair screening has no free utility oracle

**Disposition:** zero new IDs. Refine HYP141/FA01, HYP002/059 and own waves011/013; no current recipe, final, or main-gate change.

**Mechanism.** Test existing pair-first allocation against label-blind seeded uniform ordering of the same complete legal AST universe. IIFE computes interaction information across pairs, then evaluates transformed candidates through downstream cross-validation; it does not establish a fit-free substitute for CatBoost utility.[1] A frozen discretized screen is our cheaper adaptation. Uniform search is a baseline, not a guarantee of discovering a useful pair.[2]

**Prediction/counterexample.** Specify twelve same-unit parents and one oriented subtraction per unordered pair: 66 legal ASTs. In eight invented user-query groups with two candidates each, only group1 purchases: a has (x,y)=(1,3), b=(1,1); others have (1,1), all nonpositive. Other parents are constant. Frozen bins [0,4) erase every parent distinction, so every discretized interaction score ties at zero, while x−y separates a from b. Reverse group1's purchased item: identical past and screen scores, opposite useful ordering. This falsifies a universal screen-to-ranking guarantee, not IIFE's estimator. If B already models the raw parents' interaction, the transformation may add nothing. Rare feedback cannot resolve that by declaring the proxy correct.

**Nearest finite UNRUN falsifier.** Write these two literal outcome worlds and a predeclared tie order. Check pair enumeration, constant-bin scores, selected AST identities, expanded NULL/support closures and reversed ordering. Do not fit or simulate a CatBoost quality result. One world has 8 Q/16 C rows/1 positive group; both require at most 384 parent values and 2112 pair-row histogram updates. Record all 66 label-dependent pair scores, not merely selected children.

**Strong control/task1 benefit.** Freeze the legal grammar before labels; legality is distinct from the visited subset. Compare pair-first and uniform policies under the same total-cost ceiling and explicit feedback/fit caps, Q/C/full-Y targets, source availability, typed/time/NULL semantics, model recipe and final selection rule. Uniform need not waste saved screening time; it may explore within the same caps. Eligible B/W procedures remain quality controls on the same future context; their preparation/training/scoring costs are not free. Winning only against uniform does not establish gain over B/W. This isolates useful allocation from manual inventory or extra opportunities.

**Cost/negative outcome.** Pair discovery costs O(Np²), histogram state up to O(p²b²); dense candidate storage adds O(Np²). Charge bin fitting, complete historical prerequisites, authentication, masks, spills, all proxy/validation looks, reused-label feedback and failed fits. Labels mature before screening; bins/policy exist before application. No current experiment/grant; future reservation unknown. If uniform matches, the screen discards useful pairs, or no incremental B/W gain appears, defer HYP141 rather than expand feedback.

[1] [IIFE v1, Algorithm3](https://arxiv.org/html/2409.04665v1).
[2] [Bergstra–Bengio2012](https://jmlr.org/papers/v13/bergstra12a.html).
